topics.why_in_news: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change notified Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 replacing SWM Rules 2016 to strengthen segregation, recycling and circular-economy based waste governance.
prelims_quick_notes: SWM Rules, 2026 notified under Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
Rules replace Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016.
Focus on circular economy and waste minimisation.
Extended Bulk Waste Generator Responsibility (EBWGR) introduced.
Landfill dependency to be reduced through recycling and RDF usage.
Digital monitoring and compliance systems strengthened.
important_facts: Wet waste processed through composting or biomethanation.
Dry waste routed to Material Recovery Facilities (MRFs).
RDF stands for Refuse Derived Fuel.
Bulk Waste Generators identified using area, water-use and waste-generation criteria.
CPCB issues compensation guidelines under rules.
Legacy dumpsites require biomining and bioremediation.
Rules apply Polluter Pays Principle and Extended Producer Responsibility concepts.
key_highlights: RDF substitution targets imposed on industries.
Special waste-management provisions made for hilly and island regions.
Carbon-credit generation encouraged for local bodies.
exam_relevance: Important for Environment, Urbanisation and Governance.
Useful for circular economy and waste-management topics.
Can be linked with climate mitigation and sustainable cities.
prelims_traps: SWM Rules, 2026 notified under Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
MRFs are sorting and recycling centres.
Polluter Pays Principle incorporated in waste-governance framework.
